entry_sequence.transcript_quote: Once we get a clean break above pre-market highs or below pre-market lows, this is your first signal.
entry_sequence.action: Wait for a clean break above the pre-market high or below the pre-market low.
entry_sequence.rationale: The break confirms the initial directional bias.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: I personally like the retest, but depending on this scenario, I might take the breakout trade.
entry_sequence.action: Wait for the price to retest the broken pre-market level (for a long entry) or wait for the price to break and retest the opposite side (for a short entry).
entry_sequence.rationale: The retest provides a higher probability entry after the initial break.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: So if you were the breakout trader in this scenario, you would go long at the close of this two-minute candle.
entry_sequence.action: Enter long at the close of the 2-minute candle after a clean break above the pre-market high.
entry_sequence.rationale: The close confirms the breakout momentum.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: You want to wait for the close. You want to see the volume elevation. Ideally, looking at order flow as well.
entry_sequence.action: Confirm the breakout/retest with an increase in volume and ideally look at order flow.
entry_sequence.rationale: Volume elevation confirms the validity of the breakout or retest.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: Your stop loss is going to be below the breakout candle.
entry_sequence.action: Place the stop loss below the breakout candle (for long) or above the breakout candle (for short).
entry_sequence.rationale: The stop is placed beyond the candle that confirmed the entry.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: A liquidity sweep is going to be a brief fake out below or above the level.
entry_sequence.action: Wait for a liquidity sweep (brief fake out below the pre-market low or above the pre-market high) to trigger a reversal.
entry_sequence.rationale: The sweep sets up a powerful move in the opposite direction.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: If we go back to our chart and we go ahead and we look at this example right here, essentially what's happening with a liquidity sweep is some people are going to look to go short below this pre-market low or London low or anybody who has long previously might have a stop-loss set right below this area.
entry_sequence.action: Enter long after a liquidity sweep of the pre-market low (London low) is confirmed by a strong reversal candle.
entry_sequence.rationale: The sweep triggers a stop-run, setting up a reversal move in the opposite direction.
